I will keep my land mainly in the wheat-maize cycle because that is what I know best and it feeds my cash flow steadily across the year. I have 14 mu and only two people in the household, so I will not spread myself too thin with too much cotton. I will put 10 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same 10 mu, and I will keep 4 mu in cotton. I will use improved wheat seed because it is stable and familiar, hybrid maize because maize responds well and gives me stronger yield, and improved cotton seed rather than anything too risky. Since I have well irrigation, I will use water at the key times instead of irrigating too often, because pumping costs money and I farm carefully. I will fertilize wheat and maize more heavily than cotton because they are my main rotation crops and give me the more dependable output. I will use rotary tillage for wheat and cotton because it is manageable for me, and I will use no-tillage for summer maize after wheat harvest to save labor and catch the season on time. I will spray when needed but not excessively, keeping wheat and maize moderate and cotton a bit higher because cotton usually needs more pest control here. This is the plan I would follow to keep the work within my strength, use my irrigation access well, and protect yield on the crops I rely on most.
